title: 真假金丝雀的博弈第14章
content_zh:
第14章 公开透明化方案

    周三上午，我把方案草案发到顾西辞的邮箱。

    标题写的是《关于顾氏与温女士合作关系的公开透明化方案》。这个标题我想了很久，本来写的是“温小姐”，删了改成“温女士”。小姐是别人叫的，女士是我自己挣的。

    下午三点，他叫我去办公室。

    推开门的瞬间我就觉得气氛不对。他坐在办公桌后面，面前摊着我那份草案，旁边还坐着两个人。一个是法务部的陈律，另一个是公关部的负责人，姓孙，四十岁出头，短发圆脸，说话速度很快。

    “坐。”顾西辞指了指陈律旁边的椅子。

    我坐下。孙主管看我的眼神带着三分好奇七分审视。她大概是第一次近距离接触热搜上的“合约金丝雀”。

    顾西辞把草案往前推了推：“方案我看完了。核心思路没问题——公开合作模式，消除外界揣测对项目的影响。但有两个问题需要讨论。第一个，陈律，你来说。”

    陈律推了推眼镜：“温小姐，你的方案里写得很清楚，要公开合约的核心条款、合作范围、双方权利义务。从法务角度看，合约本身有保密条款。如果要公开，需要双方书面同意解除保密义务。这一条不难，你和顾总都签字就行。但问题是——公开到什么程度？”

    “条款公开，隐私保留。”

    “具体怎么划分？”

    “公布三样东西就够了。第一，我的职务——顾氏并购项目特别顾问，以及我负责的工作内容：商业社交协助、舆情分析、非财务风险评估。第二，合约期限——三年。第三，薪酬方式——按场次计费加基础月薪。不公布具体金额，不公布合同全文。”

    陈律在记事本上唰唰地记着，点了点头：“这样可以避免法律风险。”

    “好。第二个问题。”顾西辞把目光转向孙主管，“孙姐，你来说。”

    孙主管把手里的笔转了一圈：“温小姐，我就直说了。你要公开这份合作关系，目的是为了消除外界揣测对吧？但问题是——你跟顾总之前的舆论基础已经很厚了。热搜挂了好几次，媒体给你们贴的标签是‘合约金丝雀’，是‘假千金逆袭’。你突然发官方声明说‘我们只是商业合作’，你觉得舆论会信吗？”

    “不会全信。”

    “那怎么办？”

    “让他们吵。一部分人会信，一部分人不信。不信的人会继续猜测，但他们猜的内容已经没有新料了。因为我们已经把能公开的信息全部公开了，剩下猜不到的才是真正的隐私。公众对隐私的猜测会一直存在，但那已经不是我们需要负责的部分。我们需要负责的是给合作方一个交代——方总需要看到的不是舆论平息，而是顾氏有应对舆论的能力。这份方案就是证明。”

    孙主管转笔的动作停了。她歪着头看了我几秒，然后忽然笑了一下。

    “你学过公关？”

    “没学过。被舆论打过。”

    顾西辞靠在椅背上，嘴角弯了一下。

    “那就这么定了。草案修改之后交陈律审核，孙姐负责新闻稿和发布渠道。接下来就是正式发布会的问题。”

    “等等，”我转头看他，“什么发布会？”

    “你方案里写的第四条——举办顾氏并购项目媒体沟通会，由项目特别顾问温女士主持。”

    “那是我写的建议。建议的意思是可以做也可以不做。”

    “建议被采纳了。发布会定在下周三。”

    我盯着他看了三秒。他表情纹丝不动，手指在桌面上轻轻敲着，一下，两下，三下。

    “你早就准备好了发布会，只是在等我写方案？”

    “不是等你。是确认你有没有胆子上台。”他把一份文件推过来，是发布会的筹备方案，打印好的，排版整齐，页脚标注着日期——上周五。他上周五就让人准备好了发布会方案，而我周一才交草案。他不是在等我写方案，他是在等我自己往坑里跳。

    “顾西辞，你这是挖坑给我跳。”

    “这坑是你自己挖的。你方案里写了，公开透明化方案最好的发布方式就是面对面媒体沟通会。我只是帮你把坑挖深了一点。”
content_en:
Chapter 14 Openness and Transparency Plan

    On Wednesday morning, I sent the draft plan to Gu Xici’s email.

    The title reads "Plan for transparency in the cooperative relationship between Mr. Gu and Ms. Wen." I thought about this title for a long time. It was originally written as "Ms. Wen", but I deleted it and changed it to "Ms. Wen". Miss is called by others, but I earn it myself.

    At three o'clock in the afternoon, he asked me to go to the office.

    The moment I opened the door, I felt something was wrong with the atmosphere. He was sitting behind his desk, with my draft spread out in front of him, and two other people sitting next to him. One is Chen Lu from the legal department, and the other is the head of the public relations department. His surname is Sun. He is in his early forties, has short hair and a round face, and speaks very fast.

    "Sit." Gu Xici pointed to the chair next to Chen Lu.

    I sit down. Manager Sun looked at me with a look that was partly curious and partly scrutinizing. This was probably the first time she had a close encounter with the "contract canary" on the hot search topic.

    Gu Xici pushed the draft forward: "I have finished reading the plan. There is no problem with the core idea - an open cooperation model to eliminate the impact of outside speculation on the project. But there are two issues that need to be discussed. The first one, Chen Lu, please tell me."

    Chen Lu pushed up his glasses: "Ms. Wen, your plan is very clear. The core terms of the contract, the scope of cooperation, and the rights and obligations of both parties must be disclosed. From a legal perspective, the contract itself has a confidentiality clause. If it is to be disclosed, both parties need to agree in writing to lift the confidentiality obligation. This clause is not difficult, as long as you and Mr. Gu sign it. But the question is - to what extent should it be disclosed?"

    "Terms are public, privacy reserved."

    "How to divide it specifically?"

    "It is enough to announce three things. First, my position - special consultant for Gu's M&A project, and the work content I am responsible for: business social assistance, public opinion analysis, non-financial risk assessment. Second, the contract period - three years. Third, the remuneration method - billed per session plus basic monthly salary. The specific amount will not be announced, and the full text of the contract will not be announced."

    Chen Lu scribbled on his notepad and nodded: "This can avoid legal risks."

    "Okay. Second question." Gu Xici turned to Director Sun, "Sister Sun, tell me."

    Manager Sun twirled the pen in his hand: "Ms. Wen, let me tell you the truth. You want to disclose this partnership to eliminate outside speculation, right? But the problem is - you and Mr. Gu have already had a strong foundation of public opinion. You have failed in hot searches several times, and the media has labeled you a 'contract canary' and a 'fake daughter's counterattack.' You suddenly issued an official statement saying, 'We are just a business cooperation.' Do you think public opinion will believe it?"

    "I don't believe it all."

    "What should we do?"

    "Let them argue. Some people will believe it, and some people will not believe it. Those who don't believe it will continue to speculate, but there is no new information in their guesses. Because we have disclosed all the information that can be disclosed, the rest that cannot be guessed is the real privacy. Public speculation about privacy will always exist, but that is no longer what we need to be responsible for. What we need to be responsible for is to give an explanation to our partners - what President Fang needs to see is not to calm public opinion, but that Gu has the ability to deal with public opinion. This plan is proof of it."

    Manager Sun stopped turning his pen. She tilted her head and looked at me for a few seconds, then suddenly smiled.

    "Have you studied public relations?"

    "I haven't learned anything. I've been beaten by public opinion."

    Gu Xici leaned back on the chair and curled the corners of his mouth.

    "Then it's settled. After the draft is revised, it will be submitted to Chen Lu for review, and Sister Sun will be responsible for the press release and release channels. The next step is the official press conference."

    "Wait," I turned to look at him, "What press conference?"

    "The fourth item in your plan is to hold a media communication meeting for the Gu's merger and acquisition project, hosted by Ms. Wen, the project's special consultant."

    "That's the advice I wrote. Advice means you can do it or not do it."

    "The recommendations have been adopted. The press conference is scheduled for next Wednesday."

    I stared at him for three seconds. His expression remained motionless as he tapped his fingers on the table once, twice, and three times.

    "You have already prepared the press conference, and you are just waiting for me to write the plan?"

    "It's not waiting for you. It's to confirm whether you have the courage to go on stage." He pushed over a document, which was the preparation plan for the press conference. It was printed and neatly typed, and the date was marked on the footer - last Friday. He had people prepare the press conference plan last Friday, and I only submitted the draft on Monday. He was not waiting for me to write a plan, he was waiting for me to jump into the pit myself.

    "Gu Xici, you are digging a hole for me to jump into."

    "You dug this hole yourself. It is written in your plan that the best way to release the openness and transparency plan is a face-to-face media communication meeting. I just helped you dig the hole a little deeper."
title_en: The Game of True and False Canaries Chapter 14
